accuracy.evidence: Ordinal numbers are defined as numbers that name a position in an ordered set, cardinal numbers as how many, matching the NCETM and Development Matters usage and standard dictionary definitions. Ordinal words and abbreviations first to tenth (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th ... 10th) were checked against the Oxford English Dictionary spellings. Every task answer was checked by hand: the race order by distance ahead is rabbit (0.86), cat (0.74), dog (0.62), frog (0.38), tortoise (0.20), so the frog in lane 1 is fourth; with the bus on the right the first person is Fay and the fourth is Cleo; carriages counted from the engine put the pig 1st, dog 2nd, cow 3rd, duck 5th; the 6th, 9th and 10th ducklings are indexes 5, 8 and 9 behind mother duck. Item answers were checked at the corners of their ranges (p4, m4, m7 for n = 4 and 9 or 10).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the confusions documented in research on children's ordinal number learning (Colomé and Noël 2012, 'One first? Acquisition of the cardinal and ordinal uses of numbers in preschoolers'; Fuson 1988) and EYFS guidance: ordinal taken as cardinal (the third bead vs three beads in step 1, p3, m8, challenge 'card'), counting from the wrong end (queue flip in step 3, carriages from the back in step 4, m3, challenge 'dir'), a label read as a place (lane 1 frog in step 2, m2, challenge 'label'), counting the leader (mother duck in step 5, the engine in m9, m6, challenge 'start'), and irregular words (twoth in m1, challenge 'word').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagordn is about position in an order: picking the third bead and then three beads, giving 1st to 3rd ribbons by who is ahead rather than lane number, finding the front of a queue that flips when the bus moves, seating animals by carriage counted from the engine, and finding the 6th, 9th and 10th ducklings without counting the leader. flagorder orders events in time and flagrepnum shows how many with objects; neither has ordinal place finding or a changing starting point. lab_distinct gate passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds the rule by doing: the third bead turns red alone, then any three beads turn blue, so place and amount look different; the frog in lane 1 is refused the 1st ribbon with feedback that a lane number is not a place; the bus moves and the last child becomes first; a carriage counted from the back is refused with a count-from-the-engine message; tapping the duckling one before the target asks 'Did you count mother duck?'. The text then confirms each rule.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'Yes, both mean 3' for the third bead and three beads (one red bead vs three blue beads), 'Yes, it is in lane 1' for the frog (it comes fourth), and 'Yes, first is always first' for the queue (the first person changes when the bus moves).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, each wrong option tagged with one of six messages: third is not three, check where to start counting, a lane number is a name not a place, the special words first, second, third, the leader is not counted, and a general say-the-order-words prompt. Answer order rotates between questions.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and everyday words (line up toys, a queue for the bus); the adult text names Development Matters, NC Year 1, CCSS K.CC.4 and key terms (ordinal, cardinal, position). The lab uses the young layout with big emoji, short canvas labels and plain step text. validate_lessons readability passes.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea: place words, third vs three, where to start, and the word list with short forms. Items cover naming a place (p1), people in front (p2, m4), third vs three (p3, m8), last place (p4, m7), straight after (p5, m5), irregular words (m1), lane labels (m2), queue direction (m3), the leader (m6, m9).

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android dark (every step, start and after Show me) and iPhone 13 light screenshots (wn-run-1117-1553). After the first screenshots the bead string was cut to 7 larger beads, race ribbons were moved beside the animal so 2nd and 3rd no longer overlap in adjacent lanes, children and ducklings were enlarged, and the 9th and 10th duckling labels were staggered. Number-giving buttons were replaced by Move along / Back / Pick buttons so the twin does not reveal the place.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: Move along, Back and Pick for beads, carriages and ducklings (each move announces the ordinal place, like a grown-up counting along), a button for each animal in the race, and a button for each child in the queue. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
